courses.title: OpenAPI Contract Engineering
courses.centralQuestion: What exactly does the API promise, and how can providers and consumers verify that promise?
courses.incomingBoundary: Basic programming ability, command-line familiarity, and no assumed OpenAPI experience.
courses.outgoingBoundary: A frozen API 1.1 contract, operation ledger, schema fixtures, security decisions, workflow description, compatibility policy, and provider-neutral behavioral scenarios.

courses.title: Contract-Driven API Service Engineering
courses.centralQuestion: Which application, database, worker, storage, and release mechanisms keep the public contract true under concurrency, restart, and partial failure?
courses.incomingBoundary: The immutable Course 1 API 1.1 handoff and its provider-neutral proof corpus.
courses.outgoingBoundary: A durable API 1.2 service with migrations 001–005, persistent idempotency, atomic conditional updates, stable pagination, worker recovery, artifact integrity, transactional webhook delivery, and compatible-release evidence.

courses.title: API Security Engineering
courses.centralQuestion: How does the API remain trustworthy when callers, credentials, inputs, destinations, dependencies, and networks cannot be trusted by default?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 2 API 1.2 durable-service handoff and migrations 001–005.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Security Profile 1.0, migrations 006–007, a threat-to-requirement security case, identity and authorization policy, hostile-input vectors, SSRF and webhook protections, abuse controls, and incident evidence.

courses.title: API Reliability and Observability Engineering
courses.stage: Observe, diagnose, contain, and recover the promise
courses.centralQuestion: How do operators know whether the user promise is still true, and how do they recover it without making the incident worse?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 3 API 1.2 service protected by Security Profile 1.0 and migrations 001–007.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Reliability Profile 1.0, migration 008, critical journeys, deadline and resilience policies, lifecycle controls, telemetry contracts, SLOs, alerts, runbooks, game-day evidence, and reconciliation plans.

courses.title: API Performance, Capacity, and Traffic Engineering
courses.centralQuestion: Where do time and capacity go, what is the first limiting resource, and which measured change improves the system without weakening correctness?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 4 observable and recoverable API 1.2 service with Security and Reliability Profiles 1.0 and migrations 001–008.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Performance Profile 1.0, migration 009, workload identities, benchmark evidence, HTTP and query optimizations, concurrency and cache policy, traffic controls, capacity models, and performance release gates.

courses.title: Event-Driven API Engineering
courses.stage: Extend the promise across asynchronous time
courses.centralQuestion: How can independent producers and consumers share durable facts without confusing intent, delivery attempts, processing effects, and historical truth?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 5 API 1.2 service with Security, Reliability, and Performance Profiles 1.0 and migrations 001–009.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Analysis Events API 1.0, Event Profile 1.0, AsyncAPI 3.1.0 contract, CloudEvents 1.0 profile, migrations 010–012, replay and dead-letter policy, and governed consumer declarations.

courses.title: gRPC and Protobuf Engineering
courses.stage: Engineer typed internal invocation and streaming
courses.centralQuestion: How should typed internal capabilities be modeled and operated when remote calls can fail ambiguously, stream for long periods, and evolve across language boundaries?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 6 HTTP API 1.2 and Analysis Events API 1.0 handoff with profiles and migrations through 012.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Analysis RPC API 1.0, gRPC Profile 1.0, proto3 executable baseline, Edition 2024 frontier, migrations 013–015, streaming protocols, method policy, and compatibility evidence.

courses.title: Distributed API Architecture and Microservices Engineering
courses.centralQuestion: When does a remote service boundary create more value than the coordination, latency, consistency, security, release, and operational costs it introduces?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 7 platform with governed HTTP, event, and RPC interfaces and migration history through 015.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Distributed Architecture Profile 1.0, explicit service and data ownership, versioned projections, saga and trust policies, independent release choreography, extraction evidence, and a GraphQL boundary brief.

courses.title: GraphQL Schema and Runtime Engineering
courses.centralQuestion: How can clients select graph-shaped data and operations without moving business ownership, authorization, cost, or consistency into an uncontrolled gateway?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 8 distributed architecture handoff with explicit service, data, contract, and trust boundaries.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Analysis Graph API 1.0, GraphQL September 2025 schema, persisted operation registry, resolver ownership, demand policy, resumable subscriptions, compatibility gates, and platform-publication metadata.

courses.title: API Platform, Governance, and Developer Experience Engineering
courses.stage: Operate APIs as an organizational platform
courses.centralQuestion: How can an organization make trustworthy API work easier to discover, create, publish, consume, evolve, support, and retire without centralizing domain ownership?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 9 handoff containing HTTP, event, RPC, distributed-service, and GraphQL contracts with explicit ownership and release evidence.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Analysis API Platform 1.0, a governed catalog and registry, lifecycle and policy engine, golden path, documentation and sandbox, SDK and provenance publication, runtime reconciliation, support model, and a ten-course graduation dossier.
